title.provenance: An ACT concerning safety. Be it enacted by the People of the State of Illinois, represented in the General Assembly:

pfas_definition.provenance: Intentionally added PFAS chemical means a PFAS chemical that a PFAS manufacturer has intentionally added to a product and that has a functional or technical effect on the product.

type.provenance: On and after specified dates, no person shall sell, offer for sale, distribute for sale, or distribute for use in the State specified products that contain intentionally added PFAS chemicals.

date.provenance: On and after January 1, 2025, no person shall sell, offer for sale, distribute for sale, or distribute for use in the State any product in any of the following product categories if the product contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical

who.provenance: On and after January 1, 2025, a PFAS manufacturer of cookware sold in this State that contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical in the handle of the cookware or in any surface of the cookware that comes into contact with food, foodstuffs, or beverages shall list the presence of PFAS chemicals on the cookware's product label.

action.provenance: On and after January 1, 2025, no person shall sell, offer for sale, distribute for sale, or distribute for use in the State any product in any of the following product categories if the product contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical.

products.provenance: On and after specified dates, no person shall sell, offer for sale, distribute for sale, or distribute for use in the State specified products that contain intentionally added PFAS chemicals.

value: sale or resale of a used product
a product sold or resold before the effective date of this amendatory Act
a product that contains no intentionally added PFAS chemical
exceptions.provenance: On and after January 1, 2025, a PFAS manufacturer of cookware sold in this State that contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical in the handle of the cookware or in any surface of the cookware that comes into contact with food, foodstuffs, or beverages shall list the presence of PFAS chemicals on the cookware's product label. Cookware is exempt from this Section if it meets all of the following requirements: (1) The surface area of the cookware is not large enough for a product label that meets the requirements of subsection (f) to be affixed to the item. (2) The cookware does not have any of the following: (A) An exterior container or wrapper upon which a product label can appear or be affixed. (B) A tag or label to which information about the cookware may be attached.
